analysis.title: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics Risk Reduction. Week Ahead. Cloud Revenue Growth. 2 Nov 2026
key_insights: Markets rebounded Monday after a rough end to last week. KOSPI rose 2% and Tokyo Electron rose 5% after beating numbers and guiding to 87% operating profit growth. Oil fell 3% as diplomatic channels stay open. Kioxia fell another 15%, so the rebound is not indiscriminate.
The open debate is whether AI economics are deteriorating or crowded positions are being forcibly liquidated. The author sees broad de-grossing of AI longs with substantial risk reduction reported.

Quant funds had their worst week since Dec 2023, with the GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate down 2.17%. US prime brokerage data is more nuanced. Fundamental L/S net exposure recovered only to the seventh percentile, mostly through index short covering.

Single stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week, driven by long sales. Macro products were net bought for a 2nd straight week. AAII Bull-Bear is negative again and CNN fear/greed is in the 20s, so the author says sentiment and positioning have been reset.
Hyperscaler cloud growth was strong: Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%. Negative free cash flow, equity raises and rising leverage have raised questions about returns on capital.

Intel fell 29% on Friday. The author reads its warning as being about consumer PCs, margins and manufacturing rather than AI demand. Amazon went from down 7% pre-market to close down only 1.4%, despite free cash flow concerns, because it is a well-owned position.

The AI debate is circular. One camp says power and data center build-out cannot support 2027 spending, so picks-and-shovels growth rolls over. The other says compute will be overproduced and rental economics will be destroyed. Demand is strong, but the return on the next trillion dollars of investment is less certain. In crowded positioning every new concern becomes a reason to de-risk.

Midterms are tomorrow. Historically the period after US midterms has been positive for equities, since removing uncertainty often matters more than the outcome. Much of the worry is already in positioning. The author expects getting the event behind us to be constructive.

Oil/Iran: diplomatic overtures through Qatar continued over the weekend and talks remain alive, but there is no agreement. The range of outcomes is wide. It is unclear whether the diplomatic window survives the elections or the US returns to escalation afterwards.

The Treasury quarterly refunding announcement (QRA) on Wednesday may be underappreciated. The question is whether Treasury offers duration relief through smaller long-end auctions, more buybacks or a shift toward bills. Long-end cuts were not explicitly raised in the dealer questionnaire, so an immediate reduction is less certain. A constructive surprise could help duration and growth equities, while unchanged issuance could disappoint.

BoE: Thursday's 25bp hike to 4% is almost fully priced. The question is whether Bailey validates the three to four further hikes priced over the next year. The author finds that aggressive given weakening growth, though energy inflation is the risk, and leans toward the market overpricing the full tightening cycle.

Key events this week: ISM manufacturing and Apple tonight (iPhone demand and early Duo orders), AMD tomorrow (critical after Intel), Arista (AI networking read), and Friday's NFP with consensus around +65k, unemployment 4.2% and wages +0.3%.

Last week looked like wholesale de-grossing: momentum unwinding, most-shorted names squeezing, leverage coming out, defensives and quality strong while AI multiples compressed. The market is pricing an abrupt growth slowdown, stalling AI capex, lower nominal growth and rates, and a premium for quality balance sheets.

The author sees nothing in last week's hyperscaler results suggesting weaker spending intentions, and says AI monetization continues to improve. Nobody wants to add risk given repricing cost of capital, political events and protection of strong YTD gains. The author's gut call is a painful year-end rally that is under-owned, poorly participated in and impossible to chase, but thinks events need to clear before risk is added.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler cloud growth was extraordinary (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%). Nothing in last week's results suggested spending intentions were weakening, and AI monetization continues to improve. Positioning and sentiment have been reset.
tension_points.bear_case: Negative free cash flow, equity raises and growing leverage requirements raise questions about returns on capital. The return on the next trillion dollars of investment is less certain, and each new concern gives crowded holders a reason to de-risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AMD's results tomorrow are called critical after Intel's warning. Weak AI demand there would support the deteriorating-economics reading.

tension_points.bull_case: One camp argues power and data center capacity cannot keep up with 2027 spending, which supports demand for suppliers.
tension_points.bear_case: The other camp argues compute will be overproduced, destroying rental economics and forcing lower multiples. Both camps also expect multiple compression for picks-and-shovels names.

tension_points.bull_case: Smaller long-end auctions, more buybacks or a shift toward bills would give duration relief, which could help duration and growth equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-end cuts were not explicitly raised in the dealer questionnaire, so unchanged issuance is possible and might disappoint.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wednesday's QRA decides it: unchanged long-end issuance would undercut the relief case.
